## R1 Microsoft full-CredSSP memory-BIO pump repair — 2026-10-26

**Assignment-time main:** `ddba1f369f9a5cb3756610a7119e20a8bf864666`; **reconciled publication parent:**
`420a91168ae0faffc2c5decc744aaad44b9b6f42`. Owner-supplied Linux/X11 baseline is **989/989 CTest PASS**.

R1 audit found no production TLS transport defect. The Windows full-`CREDSSP`
test harness was lock-step: it required non-empty peer output every round and
spun server OpenSSL operations internally. That can terminate at
`server-initial-tsrequest / SEC_I_CONTINUE_NEEDED` even when SSPI has retained
stream state or OpenSSL has residual/post-handshake bytes.

The test-only repair replaces those assumptions with one bounded pump shared by
the portable-name, IP-SPN and bare-IP cases. Whole SSPI tokens are fed to the
server BIO, all server BIO output is drained, one OpenSSL operation runs per
iteration, TLS Ready can flow directly into residual application data,
`SECBUFFER_EXTRA` and `SEC_E_INCOMPLETE_MESSAGE` lifetimes are preserved,
and an empty-output continuation is allowed only from SSPI-owned state. Every
iteration records the five requested progress facts and bounded
BIO/`SSL_pending()`/application details; termination is boundary, typed
failure, true no-progress or round limit. Negotiated TLS version is reported;
no production TLS version or wire profile is changed.

test-only sequencing mismatch before qualification: the round that completed
`SSL_do_handshake()` could also enter the application reader. The correction
defers that application read/write work to the following bounded pump
iteration, so a TLS-ready transition performs exactly one OpenSSL provider
operation while residual BIO/`SSL_pending()` bytes remain available without
requiring new wire input.

## R9/R10 same-port restart diagnosis and correction — 2026-10-24

**Starting exact-main parent:** `0dd28a0a6840eb343b1dae4fa13ec2d9f73ea00c`.

Exact-SHA Actions run `40129269378` compiled the corrected DirectNtlm
lifecycle successfully. In focused sanitizer job `120977311045`, the
malformed peer was retired, the next valid peer completed the real
DirectNtlm/CredSSP path and was denied at the expected native
`Admission` boundary. The fixture then failed at
`tests/test_linux_runtime_direct_ntlm_lifecycle.cpp:1196` when immediate
Stop -> fresh Start attempted to reuse the same configured port.

Source review isolated the remaining boundary to POSIX listener lifetime.
`OwnedLanListener::close()` correctly closes the listening descriptor, but
`openLanListener()` previously bound a new POSIX socket without
`SO_REUSEADDR`. Because R2 rejection actively closes the accepted server-side
connection, its local endpoint can remain in `TIME_WAIT`, making the
immediate exact-port bind report occupied. This is why the older same-port
three-cycle TLS fixture could pass while the stronger server-rejection
lifecycle failed.

The correction sets only POSIX `SO_REUSEADDR`; Windows retains
`SO_EXCLUSIVEADDRUSE`. No `SO_REUSEPORT` is enabled. A dedicated native
CTest now drives accept -> server active close -> peer EOF -> listener close ->
same-port immediate rebind and separately confirms another live duplicate bind
still returns `PortOccupied`. The focused R9 sanitizer lane builds and runs
that case before the DirectNtlm lifecycle.

**NOT RUN**. Exact-publication-SHA hosted qualification: **PENDING**. No
physical server/client or native desktop action was performed.

### 2. Native Runtime Audit & TCC User Experience
- **No Prompt on App Launch**:
  `MacRuntimeHostControl` creation and background service run without requesting screen capture or accessibility permissions (`runtime.macos-host-control-no-prompt-on-app-launch`).
- **TCC Permission Gating on Sharing Request**:
  - Missing Screen Recording triggers `CGRequestScreenCaptureAccess()` once and sets user-facing message: `"Screen Recording permission required. Enable Screen Recording in System Settings > Privacy & Security."` (`runtime.macos-host-control-screen-recording-permission-denial`).
  - Missing Accessibility permission when remote control is requested triggers `AXIsProcessTrustedWithOptions` prompt once and sets user-facing message: `"Accessibility permission required for remote control. Enable Accessibility in System Settings > Privacy & Security."` (`runtime.macos-host-control-accessibility-permission-denial`).
  - `DesktopWindow::requestStart` surfaces `host_.status().failure` so these actionable instructions are displayed directly in the GUI.
- **Dynamic Revocation Teardown**:
  - `serviceOnce()` inspects screen capture preflight during active sharing (`ListenerAvailable`, `ClientAuthenticating`, `ClientConnected`); if revoked, immediately tears down listener, TLS, and native session, transitions to `RuntimeHostStage::Revoked`, and records `"Screen Recording permission was revoked in System Settings."` (`runtime.macos-host-control-permission-revocation-retires-sharing`).

## R1 terminal transport-classification authoring receipt (2026-10-20)

Starting shared-main parent: `bd134d748dbccbdf2b812c7ad9e20b1ad17ff247`.

Current-main review confirmed the R10 Qt accepted-client scheduler exists and
the remaining R10X dependency is the native X11 post-Share owner, not R1 socket
ownership. R1 therefore continued with offline production transport coverage.

The review found that `LinuxRuntimeConnection::pollSocketReadinessOnce()`
revoked on `POLLERR` before the existing R1 recv/send/OpenSSL operation could
observe an abortive peer close. That path could erase the useful peer-reset
classification as generic cancellation. The correction dispatches
`POLLERR`/ `POLLHUP` once in the requested direction and leaves
`POLLNVAL` as the scheduler-level invalid-descriptor failure.

Dedicated ordinary CTest
`runtime.linux-connection-r1-terminal-transport-classification` covers a real
TLS `close_notify`, TCP half-close without TLS shutdown, abortive RST through
the native poll path, malformed TLS during the HYBRID handshake and explicit
descriptor reuse after revoke. The expected diagnostic classes are
`OrderlyTlsClose`, `TransportError`, `TlsFailure` and `Cancelled`;
late operations must remain closed without touching the replacement fd.

Canonical local build/full CTest: **NOT RUN** in this connector environment.
Exact publication-SHA hosted CI: **PENDING**. No positive HostControl listener,

## R2 NTLMSSP fixed Version-field authoring correction (2026-10-20)

The initial NTLMSSP framing publication
`2131703acd28db77f6a6951139f18cc45fed7e01` was rechecked against the
published MS-NLMP Type 1/2/3 structures before hosted acceptance was claimed.

8-byte Version field as structurally absent whenever NEGOTIATE_VERSION was
clear. MS-NLMP keeps the field in each message layout and requires zero bytes
when the flag is clear.

the generated Type 2 Version field zero, validates zero Type 1/3 Version bytes
when their flag is clear, and moves the synthetic MIC/payload fixture after the
fixed Type 3 header. The exact Type 2 byte oracle now includes the eight zero
Version bytes. Microsoft specification review: **PASS**. Local compile/full
CTest: **NOT RUN** in this connector environment. Publication-SHA hosted CI:
**PENDING**. No live authentication, listener or GUI secret path was enabled.

R3's DELETE -> CREATE -> MAP through the existing exact-receipt TLS writer;
`Rejected` retires the native owner and connection.

The first unresolved changed geometry starts one monotonic six-second deadline.
Later RandR generations do not extend it, and a completed older MAP does not
clear it; only a subsequent fresh R3 `Unchanged` decision proves the currently
observed native geometry is mapped. The poll sleep is capped by the remaining
resize lifetime even during TLS WANT_READ/WANT_WRITE. Capture uses R5's typed
geometry/session freshness overload, so stale capture generations are never
borrowed after remap.

New ordinary offline CTests:
`runtime.linux-connection-resize-deadline-bounded-poll` and
`runtime.linux-connection-graphics-surface-remap-denials`. The positive
DELETE/CREATE/MAP wire/ACK behavior remains R3's production-backed
`transport.dvc-graphics-surface-remap`.

Local owner `~/rdp-server/build` configure/build/full CTest: **NOT RUN** in
this GitHub-connector environment. Exact publication-SHA hosted CI: **PENDING**.

ISC-licensed `gssapi/gss-ntlmssp` local NT-hash credential path is a
standards-compatible domainless candidate, but it is not integrated or proven
with Microsoft clients. Independent application password remains disabled.
The existing OS-account fallback requires a Kerberos realm/KDC, explicit
TERMSRV keytab/principal mapping and final PAM verification; a stock local
Linux password alone is not the offline fallback.

## R3 static CLIPRDR Microsoft channel-flags and reconnect generation correction (2026-10-18)

Normative MS-RDPBCGR sections 2.2.6.1.1 and 3.1.5.2.2 require ignoring incoming SUSPEND/RESUME and SHADOW_PERSISTENT flags, and support FIRST/LAST reassembly independently of the optional SHOW_PROTOCOL header-visibility bit. The R3 first increment unnecessarily rejected those harmless client flags. This follow-up keeps compression and unknown-bit denial, adds an explicit offline `transport.cliprdr-ignored-client-flags` CTest, and ensures genuinely broker-created clipboard route generations use a single overflow-safe process-wide atomic R3 allocator instead of restarting at 1 for each connection. This prevents same-channel/generation ABA across connection replacements. Full production tests for these source changes remain **NOT RUN / pending on publication**.

The preceding header-corrected source `d81bcff7` passed its Linux production R2 build and all eight new R3 CLIPRDR CTests in Ubuntu (8/8). Its ordinary Ubuntu and hosted macOS full CTests **FAILED** solely on the separately introduced R8 `clipboard.windows-clipboard-publication-midcallback-retirement` assertion at test_windows_clipboard_adapter.cpp:525; R8 owns that failure, not R3 and not an authenticated Microsoft-client session. No live clipboard/FileContents activation or deployment is permitted without real R2/R10 admission.

**Authored on current `main`; hosted CI pending.** R1's review of the
loopback listener at `4132fa7e` cleared the listener-layer dependency. This
increment moves each accepted loopback socket into one nonmoving
`LinuxRuntimeConnection` and adds a production readiness-only poll boundary.
The poll borrows R1's exact descriptor, performs no read/write/dup/close,
clamps one wait to `kMaximumTcpPollWait`, preserves current read/write WANT
direction, treats ConfigureTls as an explicit no-poll owner transition, and
uses aggregate revocation for expiry or native poll failure.

The service now serializes X.224, TLS and CredSSP through the existing
`advancePreAdmission()` owner. Only `CredentialsVerified` may call the real
`issueAdmission()`; no Boolean, UID, configured display or test fixture can
mint a lease. If genuine R2 admission succeeds, the same connection then drives
one exact first MCS TPKT through
`advancePostAdmissionMcsConnectInitial()`. The connection is deliberately
revoked after `AdmittedConnectInitial` because R10 does not yet expose the
R2-authorized MCS Connect Response / AttachUser / ChannelJoin writers in the
production service loop.

New centrally registered CTest
`runtime.linux-connection-pre-admission-native-poll` uses the production
poller on a real loopback accepted socket to prove no-event behavior, read
dispatch, write-direction transition, X.224 HYBRID confirmation, TLS-owner
transition and stale-post-revoke closure without creating a positive R2 lease.
Canonical hosted build/CTest is **NOT RUN / pending** at authoring.

candidate policy and lets RAII close the socket, so TCP acceptance remains
strictly pre-authentication and creates no R2 admission or competing SSL
reader/writer.

requires the existing secure configuration snapshot, TLS credentials,

file-descriptor budget. It accepts only serialized `max_connections=1`.

and then lets the move-only accepted socket close; TCP accept therefore remains
strictly pre-authentication and cannot grant R2/R3/native authority.

## R1 Linux buffered-TLS verification and Microsoft-client transport review (2026-10-17)

**Verified shared-main SHA:** `7ac63a255e41a9f2786629b31a1af53d2b7ab164`.
R10 repair `8d980a202eafeefd958213f65344e955ce1b2415` moved the
incomplete licensing-authority construction out of line; R9 `7ac63a25` only
synchronized assurance selectors and does not change R1 production source.
Later R2/R9 denial-only native-desktop evidence does not change R1.

Exact-SHA Ubuntu/GCC job `117431351690` passes **617/617 Debug** and
**617/617 Release**. In both configurations:
`transport.tcp-owned-buffered-tls-credssp-mcs-readiness` is #168 PASS,
`transport.tcp-owned-tls-application-cancellation` is #181 PASS, and
`runtime.linux-connection-pre-admission-dispatch` is #375 PASS.
Exact-SHA R9 Clang ASan/UBSan job `117431351644` is **SUCCESS**: its
synchronized bounded R1/R3 selector is **93/93 PASS** and includes
`transport.tcp-owned-buffered-tls-credssp-mcs-readiness`; the direct Linux
runtime-security selector is **15/15 PASS**, including the pre-admission
scheduler case.

R1 review finds no second transport defect. `SSL_pending()` is used only as a
readiness fact on the exact R1-owned SSL. R1 suppresses that fact while an
application write is pending and while a pending read's exact retry direction
is WANT_WRITE. The query performs no BIO/socket I/O, retains no caller span
and grants no CredSSP/MCS/session authority. Each runtime scheduler call
executes at most one bounded application-I/O step. A successful read consumes
a positive bounded byte count; WANT or terminal outcomes change the required
direction/status. The CredSSP reader asks for exactly the remaining DER bytes
(bounded to 16 KiB), so it cannot over-read a coalesced first MCS TPKT.

After final delegated credentials are consumed, the CredSSP reader is closed.
Only the real R2 LinuxConsoleAdmissionBroker can invoke R1's private
`completeCredSspAdmission()` after concrete native admission. The pre-admission
scheduler rejects/revokes an `AwaitMcsConnectInitial` entry rather than falling
through to R1's legacy diagnostic MCS reader. Because CredSSP already opted
the connection into R1 application byte-stream mode, that legacy direct SSL
MCS reader is also terminally fenced from becoming a second plaintext reader.

The authenticated final-CredSSP + first-MCS same-record positive case remains
**NOT RUN / BLOCKED** for two independent reasons: no owner-authorized genuine
R2 native admission environment is available here, and the current Linux
aggregate exposes `authorizeMcsConnectInitial(completeTpkt)` without a
post-admission aggregate route that reads/frames the already-buffered TPKT via
the existing R1 bounded application-I/O boundary. R10 must compose that R1
path before R3 authorization; this is not permission to add an R3 SSL reader,
wrapper transport queue, duplicate scheduler or revive the legacy diagnostic
reader.

Microsoft protocol review preserves the current interoperability posture.
MS-RDPBCGR defines HYBRID/HYBRID_EX negotiation and requires Early User
Authorization only after CredSSP completes when HYBRID_EX is selected.
MS-CSSP accepts TSRequest versions 2..6 and records Windows product behavior
that a complete TSRequest is encrypted as one TLS message block, subject to TLS
maximum-message fragmentation. Current R1 policy selects HYBRID (0x02), not
HYBRID_EX. FreeRDP issue #13549 is capture evidence only: Windows App for macOS
11.4.2 (3104) offered `0x0b`, negotiated TLS 1.3, used CredSSP v6/clientNonce
and sent final authInfo; HYBRID connected while an incorrectly early HYBRID_EX
authorization stalled before MCS. Microsoft Q&A separately reports Windows 11
mstsc captures with `0x0b` and an optional mstshash cookie; this is
non-normative and must be re-captured on the exact client build. Microsoft's live release page lists Windows App 2.0.1484.0 on Windows
(published 2026-10-13). Its macOS latest-release table still lists 11.4.2
(3104), while the same page's version history lists 11.4.3 (3115, published
2026-09-29); record the actually installed build rather than resolving that
documentation/rollout inconsistency by assumption.

**Starting reconciled shared `main`:** `ccfc9e3e22f0b0492dd5a015efc27bf1352f354d`. **Publication:** this

after an R1-owned `SSL_read_ex` completes the exact CredSSP DER frame, OpenSSL
can retain already-decrypted bytes from the same TLS record while the native

make progress.

already-decrypted application bytes from the exact owned SSL, preserves pending
write and read-WANT_WRITE direction, consumes nothing and grants no protocol
authority. The serialized Linux runtime pre-admission scheduler may use that
fact for one ordinary bounded CredSSP read when its native readable flag is
false. R2 framing, authorization, SSL ownership and every application-I/O bound
remain unchanged.

the existing native loopback TLS, CredSSP and checked-in MCS fixtures. One
logical TLS application write contains the complete CredSSP DER followed by the
first MCS TPKT. The production R1 reader stops at the DER boundary; the case
requires buffered application readiness while a zero-time native poll reports
`NoEvent`, then cancels without consuming MCS or invoking the private admission
transition. Post-cancel buffered readiness, late socket readiness and reader
replay must remain closed.

The existing runtime `linux-connection-pre-admission-dispatch` case is extended
to issue a scheduler step with `readable=false` after the first bounded CredSSP
read and require further plaintext progress from the same TLS record. Existing
`transport.tcp-owned-tls-application-cancellation` is strengthened for a
WANT-read cancellation and an unresolved bounded CredSSP write suffix, including
late callbacks after R1 teardown. Existing R3 write-replay cancellation coverage
remains unchanged.

## R4 P1 native BGRA-to-AVC420 compatibility exact-SHA receipt (2026-10-17)

**Implementation:** `162093d3f50f0c9793b1eafc2cba637c98473559`.  
**Actions:** `39023110195` — **SUCCESS**.  
**Structure guard:** `39023110193` — **SUCCESS**.

The production contract is the existing shared `FramebufferView` plus
`X264Avc420SegmentedFrameProducer::openBgraCapture()` /
`prepareBgra()`. A capture-bound producer stores one nonzero R4-local capture
epoch, requires `codedGeometry == gfxAvc420CodedGeometry(visibleGeometry)`,
and rejects stale/zero/future capture epochs before dereferencing borrowed
pixels. The accepted framebuffer is top-left row-major B,G,R,ignored-alpha,
four bytes per visible pixel, exact visible width/height, stride at least
`width*4`, and a span covering every pitched row with checked arithmetic.
Conversion copies synchronously into bounded R4-owned NV12 scratch; real x264
encoding and segmented-frame ownership complete before return, so platform
capture memory may be unmapped or replaced immediately afterward.

Three dedicated production-linked real-x264 CTests execute the contract:
`graphics.x264-native-bgra-frame-ingress`,
`graphics.x264-native-bgra-resize-recovery`, and
`graphics.avc420-capture-generation-denials`. They cover padded scanlines,
2x2 visible geometry, source-memory retirement, truncated/overflow/mismatched
layout denial, stale generation denial before pixel access, resize/rebind IDR,
normal post-delivery P-frame continuity, exact unwritten cancellation followed
by IDR recovery, terminal abort, reconnect and stale prior-generation receipt
denial. No cancellation, abort, ACK or segmented-owner behavior is reimplemented.

## R1 P1 runtime TLS verification and native-loopback readiness correction (2026-10-17; exact-SHA CI pending)

**Starting reconciled shared `main`:** `9fe503cfe03722b1145d1fc9eaf4b28a417a1c9c`.

R10's Windows synthetic credential-fixture correction is present on shared main: SID-native/private-DACL setup was centralized at `e782cd642f574e7ef45792c8fe168dfad70c8d2a`, the PowerShell ACL-module dependency was removed at `75375ccfeb7523d58d40024f783ebfe84f4db50b`, and explicit broad-principal ACE normalization landed at `4a116fb2501b7cbd5c9314d37337508fd7ed3824`.

The P1 target cases are centrally generated once from the existing `runtime_transport_case` list: `transport.tcp-owned-runtime-tls-handshake` and `transport.tcp-owned-runtime-tls-identity-continuity`. On hosted MSYS2 CLANG64 at `4a116fb2...`, Actions `39012368322`, Clang **23.1.3** / OpenSSL **3.6.5**, all three R10 private-fixture ACL tests pass first. The runtime TLS handshake then passes in the focused five-case security preflight, and both runtime TLS cases pass in the complete Debug and Release 527-test registries. The tests therefore progress beyond fixture setup into the production `RuntimeServerTlsContext` and R1 `OwnedPreauthTcpConnection` path, including real loopback handshake, exact certificate comparison, negotiation provenance, bounded application I/O and terminal cancellation. This hosted evidence does not replace the owner's same-SHA persistent MSYS2 CLANG64 run.

The required wider R1 regression sweep exposed a separate test-driver defect: `transport.tcp-native-loopback-tls` failed on Linux/GCC, macOS/AppleClang, Windows/MSVC and hosted CLANG64 at the five-second readiness assertion. The test advanced both nonblocking TLS peers once and then waited only on the server socket whenever the server was unfinished. When both peers were unfinished and the client needed to consume server-produced handshake bytes, that serialized wait could starve the client until the deadline.

This correction is test-only. The loopback fixture now records each peer's current WANT direction and performs one bounded native `select` over the union of both sockets. The next SSL step is invoked only for the peer whose current read/write readiness was observed. No production TCP/BIO/SSL source, TLS owner, certificate pinning, 18 KiB application-I/O ceiling, reader/writer authority or cancellation behavior changes. The existing dedicated `transport.tcp-native-loopback-tls` CTest remains the behavior gate; no duplicate test or executable is added.

Canonical owner `~/rdp-server/build/` MSYS2 CLANG64 execution is **NOT RUN** in this connector environment. Exact publication-SHA hosted Linux/GCC, macOS/AppleClang, Windows/MSVC, hosted CLANG64, R9 sanitizer and documentation-policy evidence are **PENDING**.

**Starting reconciled shared \`main\`:** \`04a272c8b9b52f59a24401643a46d495978d1f95\`.

handshakes. The affected existing behaviors are

\`transport.tcp-native-loopback-tls\`.

The owned-connection lifecycle now advances the server only through
\`OwnedPreauthTcpConnection::pollSocketOnce\` with
\`kMaximumTcpPollWait\` under one five-second monotonic deadline while the
client performs one \`SSL_do_handshake\` step per loop. The attached-adapter
diagnostic preserves its distinct \`PreauthTcpAdapter\` path: after one client
and one server handshake step, it waits only for the exact server
NeedRead/NeedWrite direction on the real accepted socket; after server
establishment, any remaining client WANT is waited on the exact client socket
direction. Neither fixture fabricates readable/writable readiness or sleeps
during handshake.

one-step callbacks, the 18 KiB application-I/O ceiling, authorization,
licensing and listener behavior are unchanged. Existing behavior names and

or transport surface is added.

`WindowsDxgiDuplicationOwner` graph without adding another DXGI owner,
watcher, service loop or authorization source. Terminal ordering is guard ->
input -> parent close. Parent close cancels its owned capture cycle before
parent release; a close requested from an active child callback is logically
terminal immediately but keeps the child's `unique_ptr` and parent COM
resources alive until `completeDeferredClose()` runs after the outer capture
operation returns.

production attachment still creates the existing D3D11 staging context and

generation numbers and injected callbacks remain non-authorizing.

and Release, Windows/MSVC **518/518** in Debug and Release after **55/55**

- `graphics.frame-delivery-unsent-cancellation`, `graphics.avc420-segmented-frame-unsent-cancellation`, `graphics.x264-segmented-unsent-cancel-idr`, `graphics.x264-bgra-unsent-cancel-idr`, `graphics.frame-delivery-partial-send-remains-terminal`.

R9 independently passes portable graphics **39/39**, x264/BGRA **22/22**
and RDPGFX capabilities **4/4**. The lifecycle test proves mapped surface,
prior outstanding ACKs, queue-depth observation and decoded-frame observation
survive exact cancellation. The x264 NV12/BGRA tests prove the canceled P
picture is followed by a fresh IDR, then ordinary P-frame continuity after
successful delivery. The partial-send test proves nonzero/uncertain delivery
cannot use the preserving cancel operation and remains terminal.

P2 adds no production code or CTest. The R4 frame/receipt API is already the
correct single logical publication boundary. The production gap is R3's
missing authorized DRDYNVC/Graphics DVC lifecycle and cumulative outer-byte
writer. Existing MCS user data is capped at 16,383 bytes; large R4 frames
therefore require real DVC/static-channel fragmentation. R1's bounded TLS
writer already supplies exact progress, but a zero-byte WANT retains a pending
logical write and cannot be abandoned nonterminally. Safe unsent cancellation

## R3 DRDYNVC Graphics CREATE authoring receipt (2026-10-17)

**Reconciled shared-main parent at authoring:** `6ebe2fd8d860126093ed394f37445899b4825aeb`. **Publication:** this atomic R3 code/test/roadmap increment; exact publication-SHA hosted CI is **PENDING**.

The new R3 protocol owner starts only after the existing private `ShareActivated`/R2 provenance gate resolves a joined `drdynvc` static channel. It advertises MS-RDPEDYC version 1, accepts valid client capability responses reporting version 1, 2 or 3 and negotiates down to the common v1 feature set, allocates one monotonic nonzero Dynamic Channel ID plus a separate monotonic channel generation, then sends CREATE for the exact null-terminated ANSI listener name `Microsoft::Windows::RDS::Graphics`. The correlated client CREATE response must use the same ChannelId and an exact signed 32-bit creation status: nonnegative establishes the DVC; negative is a remote rejection. Wrong MCS/static channel, malformed static-VC framing, invalid capability version, wrong command/ChannelId, duplicate response, stale generation and late receipt after cancellation cannot create or revive the channel.

Control writes use the existing R3 MCS Send Data Indication serializer and one complete uncompressed static-VC chunk. Reply and write-slice receipts are monotonic: zero accepted plaintext is retryable, positive short acceptance advances only the retained slice, and full acceptance is required before the corresponding client response becomes legal. A shared per-session DVC allocator prevents ChannelId reuse and is protocol identity/freshness only; it does not create R2 authority. The successful offline lifecycle is deliberately directly testable without a production admission lease; the only session-level fixture added is denial-only and proves pre-Share/default state cannot start Graphics DVC negotiation.

- `transport.dvc-graphics-create-response-denials`
- `transport.dvc-graphics-generation-cancellation`
- `transport.dvc-graphics-pre-share-denial`

## R3 production Demand Active profile provider (2026-10-18)

**Publication parent:** `31118f88977011c13e40893383f61abcfc29d88a`.

R3 replaces the live raw Share-ID/session-ID/source/capability argument path with
one session-owned immutable Demand Active profile. The provider emits canonical
MS-RDPBCGR Share, General, Bitmap and Order capability sets and conditionally
adds only the implemented slow-path Input and uncompressed Virtual Channel
sets. It does not advertise fast-path input/output, codecs, bitmap caches,
multimonitor, clipboard, RAIL, pointer cache, auto-reconnect or VC compression.
Demand Active `sessionId` is fixed to zero; the source descriptor is bounded
to four bytes; Share IDs use a process-wide non-wrapping 32-bit allocator.

Production preparation and consumption are both private R3 transitions reached
only through the concrete R2 broker. Slow-path Input advertisement requires the
current R2 input permission, and DVC advertisement is denied unless the
negotiated `drdynvc` static role is actually joined. A profile produced by an
offline provider has a different provider identity and cannot enter the live
`McsSessionLifecycle`.

`transport.demand-active-profile-exact-wire`,

`transport.demand-active-profile-policy-variants`,

`transport.demand-active-profile-stale-unsupported-denials`, and
`transport.demand-active-profile-immutable-lifetime`.

## R3 Confirm Active capability ownership and early-input finalization (2026-10-18)

**Authoring parent:** `a5a0ac840cf3bfe61517eaf8a24a4304c55b595f`.

MS-RDPBCGR 3.3.5.3.13.2 requires the server to process and store the
capabilities received in Confirm Active and use them to determine the RDP
subset accepted for that connection. R3 now copies the exact validated client
capability sequence into the existing Share lifecycle before R10 resets its
bounded TPKT reader. CAPSTYPE_INPUT is accepted only at the normative 88-byte
size with mandatory INPUT_FLAG_SCANCODES; R3 retains the client flags and their
intersection with the server Input flags. Post-Share slow-path input is rejected
when its event format was not negotiated.

MS-RDPBCGR 1.3.1.1 also permits the client to start sending mouse/keyboard
input once Confirm Active has been sent, before connection finalization is
complete. The Share owner now consumes such correctly routed, negotiated input
without changing finalization state and without invoking any native input sink.
R10 treats that intake as another read and therefore neither grants authority
nor turns early input into a server-write transition.

`transport.share-confirm-active-client-capability-store` and
`transport.share-finalization-early-input-ignore`. The existing
`runtime.linux-serve-share-activation-composition` source guard additionally
requires R10 to recognize the early-input intake.

## R3 authenticated RDPGFX presentation ownership (2026-10-18)

**Authoring parent:** `95333b0bddb19acebf3c690ffe3e192f45b032a2`.

The previous dependency review showed that R10 had already composed genuine
Share activation, DRDYNVC creation/CAPS and the R2-selected X11 owner, while
the first-frame path still lacked one R3-owned presentation/surface lifetime.
This increment reuses R4's existing `GfxPresentationLifecycle`; it does not
create a second surface state machine.

The R3 Graphics DVC now opens that lifecycle on its own monotonic DVC
generation, passes the exact accepted client RDPGFX capability advertisement
into it, and publishes its receipt-bound CAPS_CONFIRM followed by
CREATE_SURFACE and MAP_SURFACE_TO_OUTPUT. Surface 0 is protocol-valid and the
geometry comes from the admitted GCC Client Core values already used by the
Demand Active profile. The DVC is not `Ready` until all three application
commands have been fully accepted by R1 and their R4 receipts complete.

The production frame boundary is narrowed to mandatory ClearCodec fallback:
R10/R2 supplies only frame ID and a synchronous borrowed framebuffer. R3
prepares the R4 segmented frame against its embedded current presentation and
then moves it directly into the existing DATA_FIRST/DATA outer-record owner.
The old production API accepting a caller `GfxPresentationLifecycle`,
graphics generation/surface identity or caller-prepared frame is removed.
Zero-byte cancellation, partial-write terminal abort and exact complete
delivery remain on the existing frame receipt path.

Dedicated portable CTest:
`transport.dvc-graphics-presentation-wire`. Existing Graphics frame
zero-publication, multi-fragment delivery, header/payload partial abort, stale
receipt and Share-loss tests now use the R3-owned presentation rather than an
independent test lifecycle.

The repository-mandated local `~/rdp-server/build` configure/build/full CTest
is **NOT RUN** in this connector environment. No synthetic R2 lease, listener,
desktop, XTEST event or Microsoft client was created. Exact publication-SHA
hosted CI is **PENDING**; live first-frame evidence remains blocked on R10's
persistent post-Share R1 router/owner loop plus explicit owner authorization
for the physical X11 seat.
